statement: A garden has n flowers in a row. Flower i blooms on day bloomDay[i] and stays bloomed after that.
You want to make m bouquets. Each bouquet uses exactly k flowers that are adjacent in the row and have all bloomed, and a flower can go into only one bouquet.

Return the smallest number of days you have to wait before m bouquets can be made. If it can never be done, because m × k is more than n, return −1. The number of bouquets you can make only grows as the day increases, so binary search on the day.

examples.explanation: Each bouquet needs one flower. By day 3 the flowers at indices 0, 2 and 4 have bloomed, which makes 3 bouquets. On day 2 only two have bloomed.
4 bouquets of 2 flowers need 8 flowers, but the garden has only 5, so it is impossible.
On day 7 the bloomed flowers form runs of 4 and 2, which give only one group of 3. On day 12 all seven have bloomed, and indices 0–2 and 3–5 make two bouquets.
